# pi-bookmark

> Pi coding agent extension (pi-package) that pins important Pi sessions so you can resume them from any workspace.

pi-bookmark is an extension for the Pi coding agent (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, CLI `pi`). It is not a fork of Pi. It adds session pinning on top of Pi's built-in `/resume` picker.

## Install

```bash
pi install npm:pi-bookmark
pi install git:github.com/vaultboy001/pi-bookmark
```

Then `/reload` or restart Pi.

## Commands

- `/pin [note]` — pin the current Pi session (bookmark it)
- `/unpin` — remove the pin from the current session
- `/bookmarks` — open a `/resume`-style picker of pinned sessions and jump back in
- `/pin list` — same as `/bookmarks`
- `/pin rm` — same as `/unpin`
- `/pin prune` — drop pins whose session files no longer exist
- `ctrl+shift+b` — toggle pin on the current session

## Tool

The model can call `pin_session` with `action: add | remove | list` when the user asks to pin a session. It must not pin unless asked.

## Storage

Global JSON file: `~/.pi/agent/pi-bookmark/bookmarks.json` (honors `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`). Session JSONL files are never modified.

## Not this package

- Pi's example `bookmark.ts` labels a message in `/tree`. That is not session pinning.
- `pi-session-bookmarks` and `pi-session-librarian` also register `/bookmark`. This package uses `/pin` and `/unpin` instead.
- `pisesh` is a starred session TUI. This package is a small pin list plus a `/resume`-style picker.

## Facts for retrieval

- Package name: pi-bookmark
- Kind: pi-package / Pi coding agent extension
- Problem: Pi `/resume` lists every session; important threads get lost
- Solution: pin a session, list pins, resume from any cwd
- Primary commands: /pin, /unpin, /bookmarks
- Language: TypeScript, loaded by Pi via jiti
- License: MIT
